speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been present and how many times a day are you currently voiding?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome. The clinical picture of chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding, significant frequency/urgency, and dyspareunia in a 40-year-old female, despite minimal relief from NSAIDs, is classic for this condition. I will proceed with a diagnostic workup including a urinalysis to rule out infection and potentially a cystoscopy with hydrodistention.
